fieldMarks: 15-20 in; grouse barred brown and buff, paler and slightly smaller than Greater Prairie-Chicken.
Displaying male shows purplish (not yellow) neck sacs.
Best told from Greater Prairie-Chicken by range, since they do not overlap.
behavior: Males give a booming call on courtship display grounds; otherwise cackling and clucking notes.
May move several miles daily from roosts to feeding sites; no regular migration, though some shift between summer and winter ranges.
Eats seeds and leaves, oak leaves and acorns, waste grain in fall and winter, and many grasshoppers and beetles in summer.
habitat: Sandy short-grass prairie with sand sage and bluestem, often near low shinnery (shin) oak stands.
Visits grain fields but disappears where too much native prairie is converted to farmland.
range: Southern Great Plains of the United States (Plains, Southwest and Texas regions); now uncommon and found in a few local concentrations after serious decline.

lookalikes.name: Greater prairie-chicken
lookalikes.howToTell: Greater is larger and darker with yellow-orange neck sacs and does not share the Lesser's range.
